newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian official says bank took missing state cash.
newsitem.headline: Russian official says bank took missing state cash.

text.p: Russia's central bank head on Monday accused commercial bank Unikombank of misappropriating half a billion dollars in government money and said finance ministry officials had broken rules in their dealings with it.

Bank of Russia chairman Sergei Dubinin issued a statement saying his officials had submitted evidence to the state prosecutor after uncovering suspicious transactions by Unikombank, a medium-sized operator in the banking market.
"I have been confronted with clear symptoms of the disease...of corruption," Dubinin said.
Unikombank later issued a statement calling the charges "absurd" and accusing Dubinin of making them for "political ends", without explaining what those motives might be.
Dubinin said his accusations concerned the diversion of two large government payments in 1996 and 1997 intended for Moscow regional council and MAPO-MiG, manufacturer of the MiG fighter.
The central bank chief said former first deputy finance minister Andrei Vavilov, removed in a reshuffle four months ago, had approved the payments.
"When issuing budget funds, numerous breaches of accepted procedures and rules were committed at the finance ministry," Dubinin said.

During a supervisory check of Unikombank, the central bank found that it was one in the chain of banks through which the finance ministry forwarded state funds in the form of government MinFin bonds to Moscow region and MAPO-MiG.
When Unikombank received the bonds, it sold them but kept the proceeds.
"Unikombank's management committed a number of gross violations of MinFin bond operational rules and accounting rules," Dubinin's statement said.
"The Bank of Russia will make claims for repayment against the bank and its management, who made concrete violations in their banking business."
Dubinin said the state had lost $275 million in the Moscow region case and minimum of $237 million in the MAPO-MiG case.
Unikombank was one of Russian banks chosen by the finance ministry to underwrite Russia's first Eurobond last November.
Last summer the central bank put Unikombank into temporary administration.

Vavilov could not be reached for comment. Officials at the International Company for Finance and Investments (IFCI), the bank of which he became president after leaving the ministry, also declined to comment.
Vavilov is due to hold a news conference on Tuesday.
An early ally of liberal former prime minister Yegor Gaidar, Vavilov occupied senior positions at the Finance Ministry from 1994.
